newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. finds second suspicious envelope in mailroom.
newsitem.headline: U.N. finds second suspicious envelope in mailroom.

text.p: A second suspicious envelope was found on Monday in the United Nations mailroom and police were called to examine it, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said.

A letter bomb was discovered earlier in the day addressed to the U.N. bureau of the Arabic-language newspaper Al-Hayat. "A second suspicious envelope was found in the basement mail room and (U.S.) security has been notified," Eckhard said.

U.N. security evacuated and closed off parts of two floors of the 38-story U.N. complex earlier on Monday and the New York police bomb squad was called in along with investigators from the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

At the time of the discovery of the letter addressed to al-Hayat in the morning, U.N. officials said they examined other pieces of suspicious mail, which were not addressed to the newspaper. These turned out not to have contained bombs.
In mid-afternoon Eckhard announced the bomb squad had been called in again to investigate another suspicious envelope.
